shared_elements: upright rectangular stone slab/pillar of tan-coloured stone
relief carving worked on the broad vertical face
animal figure rendered in profile on the pillar face
carving shown in situ in an excavation with rubble/soil around the base
justification: Both are upright tan stone monoliths photographed in situ whose broad vertical face carries relief imagery including at least one profile animal, which gives them a similar overall silhouette and material feel. But A carries a single bold, almost three-dimensional high-relief form on an otherwise blank shaft, whereas B is densely covered in shallow low-relief registers — a row of quadrupeds, a woven-looking horizontal band, and several stacked creatures — so the compositional schemes and carving technique scarcely correspond.
